content.text: Before finishing, I'll run a few frames in Node with a fake DOM and canvas to catch runtime errors.

I've built the neon portal demo as a single self-contained `index.html` in the workspace, with no dependencies. Just open it in a browser.

**Testing:** I couldn't look at it, because there's no browser on this machine. What I did check: the script has no syntax errors, and it ran 200 frames in Node with a stand-in canvas without any errors. That run showed 110 particles and 42 polygons on screen at a time, out of 84 in the scene; the rest are faces turned away from the camera, which the renderer skips.

**What's in it:**
- **Renderer:** a hand-written 3D renderer that draws everything onto the full-window `<canvas id="c">`. Surfaces are shaded by a fixed light and have glowing neon edges. Objects are sorted far-to-near before drawing.
- **Scene:**
  - a two-tier platform, twin pillars, a lintel and a crown cap (6 boxes, 36 faces);
  - six spinning, bobbing octahedral crystals orbiting the portal (48 triangles);
  - a portal core: a pulsing glow with swirl arms and two counter-rotating, tilted rings;
  - a scrolling cyan/magenta grid floor with a glow under the portal.
- **Background:** a dark radial gradient with 180 twinkling stars that drift slightly as the camera turns.
- **Particles:** 110 particles rise from the platform, fade in and out, and respawn.
- **Camera:** it orbits on its own. You can also drag to rotate and use the mouse wheel to zoom.
- **HUD:** a frosted-glass panel showing "NEON PORTAL 3D" and FPS/POLYS/PARTS, with Pause/Play, Orbit ON/OFF, Reset, and a speed slider from 0 to 3×.

**Limitation:** the platform is always drawn before everything else. Simple far-to-near sorting could otherwise draw its large top face over the base of the far pillar. This works because everything else in the scene sits on top of the platform.
